title: 投资经典：债券与利率 — Day 39

questions.question: 2020 年有人买入票息不到 1% 的百年期国债，理由是「国债不会违约，所以很安全」。按久期的框架，这个想法错在哪？
options: 超长久期让价格对利率极度敏感，即使从不违约，利率上行也可能让价格腰斩
凸性对持有人有利，利率上行时能抵消掉大部分账面损失，所以风险其实很小
国债违约风险其实被低估了，长期限让政府违约的可能性大大增加
票息越低久期越短，所以这只债的问题在于回报太低而不是风险太大
questions.explanation: 久期是价格对利率的乘数：期限越长、票息越低，久期越大。零利率不消灭风险，只是把它挪进了久期——奥地利百年债在 2022 年加息中两年腰斩。凸性虽对持有人有利，但抵不过超长久期放大的下跌。
questions.question_en: In 2020 someone bought a 100-year government bond with a coupon under 1%, reasoning that 'governments don't default, so it's safe.' Using the duration framework, what's wrong with this?
options_en: The extremely long duration makes the price hypersensitive to rates, so even without any default, rising rates can halve its value
Convexity favors the holder and offsets most losses when rates rise, so the risk is actually small
Sovereign default risk is actually underrated, and a long maturity greatly raises the odds of the government defaulting
A lower coupon means a shorter duration, so this bond's problem is low return rather than high risk
questions.explanation_en: Duration is the multiplier between rate moves and price: longer maturity and lower coupon mean higher duration. Zero rates don't eliminate risk; they move it into duration. Austria's century bond halved in two years during the 2022 hikes. Convexity helps the holder but cannot offset losses magnified by ultra-long duration.

questions.question: 收益率曲线刚刚出现倒挂。按这个信号的正确用法，投资者应该怎么理解它？
options: 它是很少说错方向的概率信号，但到衰退的时滞可达 6–24 个月，不能当择时指令
量化宽松压低了长端利率，因此如今的倒挂信号比过去更加精确可靠
倒挂说明市场预期央行未来还会继续加息，所以应该缩短债券的久期
倒挂本身会引发衰退，所以一出现倒挂就应该尽快清仓股票、转向现金
questions.explanation: 倒挂不是衰退的原因，而是市场对「紧缩已经过头、央行将被迫掉头」的集体判断。它很少说错方向，却几乎不告诉你日期：历史上倒挂后股市常还能涨一年以上；QE 人为压低长端期限溢价，反而让信号更难解读。
questions.question_en: The yield curve has just inverted. Used correctly, how should an investor read this signal?
options_en: As a probabilistic signal that rarely gets the direction wrong, but with a 6–24 month lag to recession, so it is not a timing trigger
QE has pushed down long-term yields, which makes today's inversion signal more precise and reliable than before
Inversion means the market expects the central bank to keep hiking, so you should shorten your bond duration
Inversion itself causes recessions, so as soon as it appears you should sell stocks quickly and move to cash
questions.explanation_en: Inversion doesn't cause recessions; it is the market's collective judgment that tightening has gone too far and the central bank will have to reverse. It rarely gets the direction wrong but almost never gives the date: stocks have often kept rising for a year or more afterward. QE suppresses the term premium on long yields, which makes the signal harder to read, not easier.

questions.question: 关于信用利差与投资时机，哪种判断最符合 Howard Marks 的思路？
options: 利差极窄说明市场普遍认为违约风险很低，这正是配置高收益债、获取稳定收益的好时机
利差极窄时补偿最薄、最危险；利差爆炸时补偿最厚，但要看违约周期走到哪一段
利差主要由央行政策利率决定，所以只要预测对了降息时点，就能判断高收益债的买点
利差越宽说明违约风险越大，所以利差扩大时应该回避高收益债，等利差收窄后再买
questions.explanation: 利差是市场为违约、流动性和风险厌恶开出的价码，决定盈亏的是付了什么价：同一批高收益债，250 基点是陷阱，2000 基点是机会。但宽利差不是免费午餐，衰退中常伴随真实违约上升，所以要结合违约周期判断，避免「接飞刀」。
questions.question_en: Regarding credit spreads and timing, which judgment best fits Howard Marks's thinking?
options_en: Very tight spreads show the market sees little default risk, which makes it a good time to add high yield for steady income
Very tight spreads offer the thinnest compensation and are most dangerous; blown-out spreads pay the most, but you must check where the default cycle stands
Spreads are set mainly by the central bank's policy rate, so calling the timing of rate cuts tells you when to buy high yield
Wider spreads mean more default risk, so avoid high-yield bonds while spreads widen and buy once they tighten again
questions.explanation_en: Spreads are the price the market charges for default, illiquidity, and risk aversion, and what decides the outcome is what you paid: the same junk bonds are a trap at 250 bp and an opportunity at 2,000 bp. Wide spreads aren't a free lunch, though; in recessions they come with real defaults, so you have to read the default cycle to avoid catching a falling knife.
